name: NCR Voyix Corporation

profile.description: NCR Voyix provides digital commerce software and hardware for the retail and restaurant industries, including the cloud-native VoyixPOS platform, AI-accelerated commerce applications, and payment processing, following the 2023 separation of NCR Corporation into NCR Voyix (software/retail/restaurant) and NCR Atleos (ATM hardware) [1]. Headquartered in Atlanta with roughly 13,500 employees across 35 countries, the company reported Q1 2026 revenue of $606M (down modestly YoY) while narrowing its net loss and raising FY2026 free cash flow guidance under CEO James G. Kelly, who took the helm in February 2025 [1][2].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): NCR Voyix launched a cloud-native, edge-enabled, microservices-based VoyixPOS platform in November 2025 — replacing 140 years of legacy hardware-centric architecture — representing a genuine software-led transformation, though revenue is still declining overall and the transformation is not yet validated by growth [1][3]. AI Deployment (2/2): The company shipped an 'AI-accelerated application suite' on the Voyix Commerce Platform and uses AI/computer vision to help retailers combat theft and shrink — concrete AI products in market with named capabilities [3]. Market Share (0/2): NCR Voyix is defending its enterprise retail/restaurant installed base against faster-growing cloud-native rivals Toast, Block/Square, and Lightspeed, with only 2% ARR growth reported — a legacy incumbent holding position, not gaining share [3]. Product Pipeline (2/2): VoyixPOS is a specific, already-shipped platform with named cloud-to-edge capabilities, not a future promise [3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D-to-revenue figure relative to peers was found.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): NCR Voyix's positioning as a 'unified commerce' provider for restaurants and retailers is functional and generic, interchangeable with any enterprise commerce software vendor [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific charitable programs or community investment figures were found. Employee Retention (0/2): CEO James Kelly has driven deliberate culture changes — ending the key-card requirement for the executive wing and personally engaging staff in a practice employees call 'getting Jim'd' — but no hard turnover or tenure data exists to score this item [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): Only RSU vesting and a gift-to-spouse transaction were found for CEO Kelly in 2026; no open-market cash purchases signaling personal conviction were identified [2].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored: D/E of 116% is above the 70% target but well below the 300% floor, scoring 0.80. ROE of 5.38% is well below the 15% target, scoring 0.36. Revenue growth YoY of -4.65% (FY2025 vs FY2024) scores 0.51 against the -20%/10% floor-target range. Forward P/E of 8.91x clears the 20x target easily, scoring 1.0. Profit margin of 2.76% is far below the 20% target, scoring 0.14. Revenue 5yr CAGR and PEG were unavailable (the 2023 NCR Atleos spinoff makes 5yr trailing figures non-comparable) and excluded. Weighted sum of 3.17 against 6 available weight units yields 5.3, rounding to 5. Liquidity floor cleared: 2.49M avg vol × $8.21 = $20.5M daily [4].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): NCR Voyix's core POS/commerce software business faces real substitution risk from AI-native, cloud-first rivals — Toast, Block/Square, and Lightspeed can iterate faster and bundle POS, payments, and CRM more nimbly than the legacy Voyix architecture, and the company's weak balance sheet (negative FCF of -$288M, Altman Z-score of 1.36) constrains reinvestment capacity to keep pace [3][4]. Switching costs across thousands of large enterprise retail/restaurant locations provide a partial moat, and 2% ARR growth shows some retention resilience, but the risk is real and analyst-flagged, not hypothetical. AI Opportunity (1/1): NCR Voyix ships an AI-accelerated application suite and AI-powered computer-vision theft prevention directly to customers on the Voyix Commerce Platform — concrete AI products in market, qualifying for the opportunity point even without a disclosed dollar figure [3].

infinite_game.summary: NCR Voyix is a 140-year-old incumbent in the midst of a genuine but unproven software-led reinvention. New CEO James Kelly has made real, specific cultural changes to open communication and is accepting near-term revenue pain for a cloud-native future, but the company has not articulated a Just Cause beyond commerce software, and no evidence of favorable competitive framing toward rivals was found.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): No distinctive Just Cause was found beyond providing commerce technology to retailers and restaurants; the company's public narrative centers on platform modernization and financial stabilization rather than a resilient, service-oriented vision [1][3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Kelly's specific, described actions — ending the executive-wing key-card policy, informally pulling employees into 'getting Jim'd' collaborations, and personally meeting with 72 restaurant customer CEOs — are genuine, concrete evidence of building open communication, though the culture shift is recent (since Feb 2025) and unproven over a full cycle [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence was found of NCR Voyix framing Toast, Square, or Lightspeed as worthy competitors to learn from; public commentary focuses on internal execution and retention metrics rather than competitor-driven self-improvement [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): The 2023 separation of legacy NCR into NCR Voyix (software) and NCR Atleos (ATM hardware), followed by the November 2025 launch of a fully cloud-native, edge-enabled microservices POS platform replacing the prior hardware-centric architecture, is a genuine, transformative reinvention of the business model [1][3].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): CEO Kelly is executing a multi-year software-led transformation while accepting real near-term financial pain — FY2025 revenue declined 4.65% and free cash flow was -$288M — in pursuit of a cloud-native future, a costly bet on long-term repositioning over short-term optics [1][4].

investment_thesis: NCR Voyix trades at 8.91x forward earnings amid an ongoing turnaround from legacy POS hardware vendor to cloud-native commerce software company. Q1 2026 results showed the net loss from continuing operations narrowing to $2M from $21M a year earlier, Adjusted EBITDA rising to $78M, and recurring revenue growing to $419M from $404M — early signs of stabilization [1]. FY2026 guidance calls for Adjusted free cash flow of $190-220M, implying 40-62% growth versus 2025, and the newly launched cloud-native VoyixPOS platform and AI-accelerated application suite give the company concrete, shipped products to sell into its large enterprise retail/restaurant installed base [1][3]. CEO James Kelly's deliberate cultural reset — ending exec-wing access barriers and personally engaging 72 customer CEOs — signals a genuine attempt to rebuild both internal trust and customer relationships [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is substantial. FY2025 revenue declined 4.65% to roughly $2.69B, profit margin is a thin 2.76%, ROE is just 5.38%, and D/E of 116% reflects a leveraged balance sheet with $1.38B in debt against only $231M cash — a net debt position of roughly $1.15B [4]. Negative free cash flow of -$288M and an Altman Z-score of 1.36 point to elevated financial-distress risk if the software transition stalls [3]. NCR Voyix faces intensifying, analyst-flagged competition from AI-native, cloud-first challengers Toast, Block/Square, and Lightspeed, which can out-innovate the legacy platform, and the company's own AI Risk Protection score of just 4/9 reflects that this is a real, not hypothetical, threat [3]. Pension-related litigation dating to 2015 was only settled in April 2026, an overhang finally resolved but reflective of the company's legacy-liability baggage [4].
key_catalysts: Continued Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow improvement toward FY2026 guidance of $190-220M would validate the software-led turnaround and support debt reduction [1]
VoyixPOS and AI-accelerated application suite adoption driving ARR growth beyond the current 2% pace, demonstrating competitive resilience against Toast and Square [3]
Further deleveraging of the $1.38B debt load as free cash flow inflects positive, reducing the Altman Z-score distress signal [3][4]
key_risks: Elevated financial distress risk — Altman Z-score of 1.36, negative free cash flow of -$288M, and net debt of roughly $1.15B against a low-margin (2.76%) business leave little room for execution missteps [3][4]
AI-native competitors Toast, Square, and Lightspeed are structurally faster-moving and could continue eroding NCR Voyix's enterprise retail/restaurant share despite switching-cost protection [3]
FY2025 revenue decline of 4.65% and ROE of just 5.38% show the software transformation has not yet translated into top-line growth or superior capital returns [4]
